title: Chunking
summary: Chunking splits each page into passages small enough to embed and to show as a citation. It packs whole sentences into a chunk until a token budget (160 by default) is reached, then starts the next chunk with the last sentences of the previous one (up to 40 tokens of overlap). Pages go in, a list of `Chunk` records with stable ids like `travel-policy.en.pdf#p2-c0` comes out. Chunk size is a core RAG trade-off: small chunks are precise but lose context, large chunks keep context but blur the embedding.

key_ideas.explain: Cutting at fixed character offsets splits sentences in half, so the embedding and the quoted answer get broken fragments. Packing whole sentences keeps every chunk readable and every quote complete.

If a fact sits at a chunk boundary, the sentence before it may be the context that makes it findable. Repeating the last ~40 tokens at the start of the next chunk means a boundary never hides that context.

Embedding models read subword tokens, not words. Arabic words often split into several tokens, so a word count underestimates length. Counting with the embedder's own tokenizer guarantees a chunk never exceeds what the model actually sees.
The id `<doc>#p<page>-c<n>` depends only on the document, page and position, so citations, evaluation gold labels and the browser index all refer to the same chunk across runs.

blocks.note: The module docstring describes the algorithm in plain words: pack sentences up to `max_tokens`, start the next chunk with the last sentences of the previous one up to `overlap_tokens`, count tokens with the embedding model's tokenizer when possible, and split any single sentence that is too long on word boundaries.
`from __future__ import annotations` makes every type hint a lazy string. You can then write `list[str]` or `str | None` on older Pythons (3.8, 3.9) and name a class inside its own body.

Imports `Page` (the input type) and `detect_language`, which tags each chunk as Arabic or English.

`_SENT_END` is the sentence boundary regex, used with `re.split`. Two alternatives: whitespace that follows `.`, `!`, `?`, the Arabic question mark `؟` or the CJK full stop `。` (the lookbehind `(?<=...)` checks the punctuation without removing it, so the sentence keeps its full stop), **or** one or more newlines. Newlines count as boundaries because Markdown headings, list items and paragraphs are separate units.
`_HEADING` matches Markdown heading markers at the start of a line (`# `, `## `). They are removed so a heading becomes plain text like "Leave policy" instead of "## Leave policy".

A **type alias**: `TokenCounter` is any function that takes a string and returns an int. Chunking does not care whether that is the e5 tokenizer or a simple regex count, which is how tests run without a model.

`simple_token_count` is the fallback counter: every run of word characters is one token, and every single punctuation mark is one token. It is a rough stand-in for a real tokenizer, used when the embedder has no `count_tokens` (the test `HashingEmbedder`). Lines 26 and 27 are blank.
`@dataclass(frozen=True)`: chunks are immutable records, so nothing downstream can edit a chunk's text after its embedding was computed.

`chunk_pages` signature. Defaults are 160 tokens per chunk and 40 tokens of overlap, and the counter defaults to `simple_token_count`. `RAGPipeline.add_pages` passes the e5 tokenizer instead. 160 tokens is well under e5-small's 512-token limit, which keeps each chunk focused on a topic or two: a large chunk averages many topics into one vector and matches every question a little and none of them well.
Guards a configuration error. If the overlap were as large as the chunk, the next chunk could start where the previous one started and the loop would never advance.
The result list for all pages.
